target_api: of_count_phandle_with_args, kcalloc (allocation/lookup APIs whose failure must propagate as an error code)
post_operation: assign a non-zero error code to the function's return variable (e.g. ret = -ENOENT / ret = -ENOMEM) before goto cleanup
path_conditions: Failure branch where an allocation/lookup returns NULL or 0 and control flows via `goto end;` to the function's tail. On entry to that goto, `ret` has not been assigned a non-zero error code on this branch, so the function returns whatever stale (possibly success) value `ret` last held — leaking a silent success to the caller despite an actual failure.
notes: The buggy thermal_of_populate_bind_params() has two failure branches: (1) if (!count) goto end without ret = -ENOENT, and (2) if (!__tcbp) goto end without ret = -ENOMEM. In both, `ret` may have been last assigned by of_property_read_u32() above (could be 0 on success), so the function returns 0 (success) despite a real configuration/allocation failure. Pattern shape: int-returning function with a local `ret` variable; an early-error branch that does `goto cleanup_label;` without first assigning a non-zero value to `ret`; the cleanup tail does `return ret;`. Identical shape to err-1 (physmap_flash_remove) modulo variable name (`ret` vs `err`).
